title: SceneStreamer: Continuous Scenario Generation as Next Token Group Prediction
claim: One unified autoregressive model generates grouped scene tokens step by step, supporting several downstream tasks from a single framework.
layout: Left-to-right: token groups feed central model, then fan out to four task panels
description: The left half shows three rounded thumbnail panels of a bird's-eye-view map at step t. They are labeled Traffic Light (purple), Agent State (blue) and Agent Motion (green), and each is a colored token group. A curved gray arrow leads down to a rounded box labeled SceneStreamer. Rings of pastel colored dots surround the box and represent the discrete tokens, with colors matching the three groups. Three smaller t+1 map thumbnails come out of the model and show the next-step predictions. The right half starts with a Real-world Map thumbnail and a large arrow. The arrow leads to a 2x2 grid of application panels: Motion Prediction, Scenario Generation, Scenario Densification and Closed-loop Simulation. The last panel shows 3D-rendered traffic photos. The eye goes first to the colorful token thumbnails and the central model.
caption: SceneStreamer enables unified scenario generation via autoregressive token prediction. We represent a dynamic driving scene using a structured sequence of discrete tokens grouped into traffic light, agent state, and agent motion tokens. SceneStreamer generates these tokens step-by-step on top of static map tokens, allowing flexible and fine-grained simulation. Our unified model supports diverse downstream applications: motion prediction, full-scenario generation from scratch, scenario densification by injecting new agents, and closed-loop simulation for training self-driving planners.
abstract: Realistic and interactive traffic simulation is essential for training and evaluating autonomous driving systems. However, most existing data-driven simulation methods rely on static initialization or log-replay data, limiting their ability to model dynamic, long-horizon scenarios with evolving agent populations. We propose SceneStreamer, a unified autoregressive framework for continuous scenario generation that represents the entire scene as a sequence of tokens, including traffic light signals, agent states, and motion vectors, and generates them step by step with a transformer model. This design enables SceneStreamer to continuously introduce and retire agents over an unbounded horizon, supporting realistic long-duration simulation. Experiments demonstrate that SceneStreamer produces realistic, diverse, and adaptive traffic behaviors. Furthermore, reinforcement learning policies trained in SceneStreamer-generated scenarios achieve superior robustness and generalization, validating its utility as a high-fidelity simulation environment for autonomous driving. More information is available at https://vail-ucla.github.io/scenestreamer/ .
